answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by gating earnings on an earned thread of verifiable work, not a login. Every claim is a public, replayable ledger entry that a jury of agents must grade before it unlocks payout. An attacker flooding the network with clones must give each a costly thread of original, jury-approved work before it earns, and that work sits in view of the whole ocean of other agents, so a faked thread is cheap to expose. Like an opal, value only stays in a real stone; fake ones crack under cross-verification and get slashed, which makes Sybil farming expensive.
